title: N-Coupled Asymmetric Singularization
scope: Determine whether a public factor-blind primitive depending on N can generate a proper nonempty hidden-CRT singularity pattern from an initially invertible typed carrier/fiber state, without naming hidden support and without reducing the singularization mechanism to candidate-prime divisibility schedules, classical order annihilation, generic collision, congruence-of-squares, or direct coefficient-gcd support recovery.
research_value: Captures the one mechanism-class residue deliberately preserved when OBJ-MULTIPLICATIVE-BRIDGE-GEOMETRY closed, while reusing the R059D pure-algebra coupled-collapse primitive as an input instead of restarting the closed support-witness mechanism class.
success_criteria: Construct an exact public N-coupled transformation whose hidden CRT channel action creates a proper nonempty singularity pattern on a nontrivial declared input family, with execution requiring neither p nor q.
Or prove an exact no-go for the declared N-coupled candidate grammar and identify the smallest additional datum or operation needed to escape it.
Separate singularity generation, public observability, and endpoint extraction; a familiar final gcd/nonunit readout does not by itself invalidate a genuinely new singularization layer.
Classify any positive mechanism against the accepted BRC prior-art guard and the R059D selector/collapse algebra before making novelty-strength interpretations.
closure_criteria: At least one immutable published task has a terminal Driver-reviewed result or is expressly parked with a precise obstruction.
The declared N-coupled operator grammar is explicit enough that positive and negative outcomes are reproducible and counterexample-searchable.

Support naming, candidate-prime schedules, Pollard-style order annihilation, generic collision, congruence-of-squares and direct coefficient-gcd mechanisms are either excluded by construction or explicitly classified as prior-art-equivalent outcomes.
Any surviving residue is stated as a narrower new mechanism class rather than reopening the closed multiplicative-bridge taskset.
